sentences.text:
Applicant :- Yogendra
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

Counsel for Applicant :- Digvijay Singh Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Mrs. Sadhna Rani (Thakur),J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A. and perused the record.

This is the second bail application moved on behalf of the applicant- Yogendra with a prayer to release him on bail in Session Trial No.247 of 2019, Case Crime No.188 of 2019, under Sections 498A, 304B I.P.C. and Section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station Kotwali Kayamganj,
District Farrukhabad.
The first bail application of the applicant was rejected by this Court vide order dated 15.12.2022.

It is argued by the learned counsel for the applicant that the applicant is languishing in jail since 24.07.2019 and as per inquest report, it is clear that the deceased in the injured condition was taken to the hospital by her in-laws, hence, the prayer of bail is made.
Learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer.
From the perusal of the record, it is found that all the merits of the bail application were discussed in the first bail rejection order dated 15.12.2022.
Since then, no other ground has arisen except the ground of incarceration and it is argued by the learned counsel for the applicant that the applicant is languishing in jail since 24.07.2019.
The applicant being the husband of the deceased is the main accused under Sections 498A, 304B IPC & 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.

Yogendra vs State Of U.P. on 12 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86189779/
1
No good ground can be said to be argued to allow the second bail application.
The second bail application of the applicant is, thus, rejected.

However, the trial court is directed to expedite the hearing and decide the aforesaid case, as expeditiously as possible, without granting any unnecessary adjournment to any of the party, if there is no legal impediment.
